network.tdh.explainer.title: TDH
network.tdh.explainer.metadataDescriptio: What TDH is, how to read your own, and how it is calculated, specified, proved and checked every day.
network.tdh.explainer.intro: Every copy of an eligible card earns its whole days held, weighted by how rare the card is and multiplied by a boost for collecting sets.
network.tdh.explainer.why: On 6529.io your TDH counts toward your Level and can weight your votes in waves that vote with TDH. Independent programs compute it every day, and the results are compared in public.
network.tdh.explainer.eligible: The Memes, Gradients and NextGen count. Meme Lab cards and received xTDH do not.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.title: TDH in a minute
network.tdh.explainer.minute.hold.title: Hold.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.hold.body: Each copy you hold counts the whole days since you got it. A copy bought today starts counting tomorrow; selling it removes its days.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.weigh.title: Weigh.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.weigh.body: Rarer cards weigh more. A card’s rate is the largest edition, today FirstGM’s 3,941, divided by the card’s own edition: FirstGM itself is 1.00, and a 310-copy Meme is 12.71.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.boost.title: Boost.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.boost.body: Complete sets, seasons and Gradients raise one multiplier that applies to everything you hold. It starts at 1.00.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.example: Example: one copy of a 310-copy Meme, held for 100 whole days by a collector who also holds one Gradient, which adds 0.02 to the boost.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.diagramDesc: Three panels. Days: 100 whole days from the purchase to the snapshot, drawn as ten groups of ten days. Rate: two bars on one scale, the largest edition, 3,941 copies, and this card, 310 copies; 3,941 divided by 310 is 12.71. Boost: a scale from 1.00 to 2.04, the highest boost under today’s rule, with one Gradient at 1.02. The result is 1,296 TDH from this card.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.snapshot: TDH is computed once a day, for the last Ethereum block before 00:00 UTC. Ages are measured to that block’s time.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.reference: FirstGM (Meme #8) is the reference card: while its edition, which counts as 3,941, is the largest, one FirstGM copy held one whole day adds exactly one base TDH.

network.tdh.explainer.sources.label: Sources
network.tdh.explainer.sources.legend: P26 is the TDH-v1 specification and § a section of it; D-numbers are the owner’s decisions; DEV and BUG are the specification’s list of deviations from the old backend and of its issues. P53, P38 and P52 are validator design documents, to be published.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.title: Checked daily, in public
network.tdh.explainer.verified.body: TDH is one written rule with several independent programs behind it, and their results are compared in public every day.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.point.pro: The validators’ Rust core, a separately written program B and the Python reference each compute the same written rule, and each is tested against the specification’s 61 conformance vectors.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.point.for: A formal model, still a proposal, reproduced all 21,410 records of a real day. Machine-checked proofs show that the inner steps of a transaction cannot change anyone’s holdings, and checked counterexamples show where that stops: a mint and its burn can still make a token count, and so change balances, rates and other holders’ TDH.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.point.dai: From 16 October 2026 the Rust core and the Python reference run beside 6529.io, and every difference is counted and classed in public. About 23 October 6529.io switches to the Rust core.

network.tdh.explainer.faq.sale.title: Why can selling one card reduce TDH by more than that card’s score?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.sale.body: The sold copy stops contributing its holding days. If the sale also breaks a set or removes a Gradient boost, your multiplier falls on the rest of your holdings too. TDH is recalculated from what you hold; it is not a permanently banked balance.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.transfer.title: Do I keep my holding time when I move a card?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.transfer.body: Moves between wallets of your confirmed consolidation keep the original acquisition time. A move outside that group removes the sender’s contribution and starts a new holding period for the recipient. Under TDH-v1 (rule version tdh-v1.0) an identity counts up to three wallets. 6529.io’s backend can also count a fourth wallet linked after an activation date, as the consolidation guide explains; the TDH-v1 specification does not include the fourth wallet yet. Delegation alone does not consolidate wallets.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.new.title: When does a new purchase or newly minted card count?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.new.body: A copy needs a completed 24-hour holding period to contribute holding days. Newly minted Memes and Gradients also need to pass the snapshot’s separate 24-hour mint-age filter. An already eligible card can complete a set before its new owner has held it for a full day.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.set.title: Does a full collection include the current season?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.set.body: Yes. You need every Meme card eligible for that snapshot, including eligible cards from the current season. When a new card becomes eligible, a previously complete collection may become incomplete. Individual season bonuses follow the eligible seasons listed above.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.rate.title: Why isn’t tomorrow’s change exactly my daily rate?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.rate.body: Daily rate is a guide calculated from positive-age copies and the current boost. Whole-day boundaries, per-token rounding, transfers, new eligible cards and changes in rates or boosts can all affect the next snapshot. The displayed rate may also be rounded down elsewhere in the app.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.xtdh.title: Where does xTDH fit?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.xtdh.body: xTDH is calculated separately. Receiving xTDH does not increase the base TDH explained here. Your TDH rate is an input to the xTDH system.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.title: Glossary
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.intro: The words these pages use, in the order a calculation meets them.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.tdh.def: Total Days Held: whole days held, weighted by rarity and multiplied by the boost, summed over everything you hold.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.cycle.def: One day’s calculation. Cycle N closes at 00:00 UTC of its date; N is the number of days since 1 January 1970.
The last Ethereum block before a cycle’s 00:00 UTC. Holdings are read as of this block, and ages are measured to its time.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.edition.d: How many copies a card counts for its rate: the larger of the copies minted and the mint limit of its claim, the limit capped at 310. Burns do not reduce it.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rate.def: How much one copy-day of a card weighs: the largest Meme edition divided by the card’s edition, rounded to cents. Older pages call it the HODL rate or edition weight.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.base.def: A card’s whole days times its rate, rounded to a whole number, before the boost.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.boost.def: One multiplier for everything a collector holds, from 1.00, raised by complete sets, seasons and Gradients.
One collector as TDH counts them: a single wallet, or a group of consolidated wallets.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.consolida: Wallets that confirm each other on the delegation contract, so they count as one identity.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.sink.def: The registry’s sinks: the zero address and 0x…dead in tdh-v1.0. Copies sent there are burned; the sinks keep records but are never debited, never consolidated and never count as participants.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.xtdh.def: A separate system that builds on TDH. Received xTDH does not change the TDH on these pages.
Boost schedules 1.1 to 1.4 are 6529.io’s versions of the boost, shown under Current boosts and Historic boosts. TDH-v1 is the exact written rule; tdh-v1.0 is its version, with today’s schedule.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.validator: A program, being built, that computes TDH itself every day, signs the result and agrees on it with other validators.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rust.term: Rust core, program B, Python reference
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rust.def: Three separately written programs that compute TDH-v1: the Rust core, which validators will run and 6529.io runs from the cutover; a second Rust program written from the specification alone; and the specification’s reference in Python.

network.tdh.explainer.deeper.spec.body: The exact rule, TDH-v1, in readable form: every input, formula and rounding step.
network.tdh.explainer.deeper.formal.body: The rule in Lean 4: what is proved, what turned out to be false, and what the proofs do not cover.
network.tdh.explainer.deeper.impl.title: Implementations
network.tdh.explainer.deeper.impl.body: The Rust core, program B, the Python reference and 6529.io, and how they are checked against each other.
network.tdh.explainer.deeper.verify.body: Every day, Rust, Python and 6529.io side by side: how many agree, and every difference counted and classed by its cause.
network.tdh.explainer.promise: Total Days Held: the art you hold, and how long you have held it.
network.tdh.explainer.formula.label: The formula
network.tdh.explainer.formula.text: Days times rate times boost equals TDH, for each card, summed over everything you hold.
network.tdh.explainer.strip.equal: Checked daily in public: on {date}, the Rust core, the Python reference and 6529.io agreed on all {total} collectors.
network.tdh.explainer.strip.other: Checked daily in public: on {date}, {equal} of {total} collectors were equal between the Rust core and 6529.io.
network.tdh.explainer.strip.awaiting: Checked daily in public from 16 October 2026, when the daily comparison starts.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.resultNote: The Gradient earns TDH of its own on top, from its own days and rate; a collector’s TDH is the sum over every card held.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.raw.def: Whole days held times copies, before any weighting. The rate turns raw days into base TDH.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.netting.d: Within one Ethereum transaction, each wallet’s movements of a token are added up and only the net change counts (D131). A copy that leaves and returns in one transaction never left.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.underflow: The check that no wallet ever sends a copy it does not hold. An input that fails it has no result.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.finalized: An Ethereum block that can no longer be reverted. A day has a result only once the block after its snapshot block is finalized.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.vector.de: A small test case with its exact expected values. A program conforms to TDH-v1 when it reproduces all 61 of them.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.root.def: One hash that commits to every record of a day (the cycle root), to every wallet record (the wallet root) or to the history of inputs (the history root). Equal records give equal roots.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.cutover.d: The day 6529.io switches from its current backend to the Rust core’s result, planned for about 23 October 2026 (D132).
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.classes.d: How the daily comparison sorts a difference: A, a deliberate difference from the old backend; B, an old-backend bug; C, the Rust core and the Python reference disagree; D, not yet explained.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.items.def: D132 is one of the owner’s decisions; DEV-2 one of the specification’s deviations from the old backend; BUG-15 one of the old backend’s issues. Each links to its entry on the specification page.
The two separately written programs behind the planned proofs of each day’s result (D119). Program A runs the validators’ own code; program B was written from the specification alone, and its TDH code is to become the validators’ second built-in check (D125).
